jobs.name: Garden wall
jobs.brief: Garden wall in stretcher bond: six bricks long, eight courses high, on the concrete footing. Keep every brick on the string line.

afterCourse.0: Course done. 71 mm brick + 12.3 mm bed joint = 83.3 mm per course, so twelve courses make exactly one metre. Next course starts with a half brick, so no vertical joint sits on top of the one below. That's stretcher bond.
afterCourse.3: Halfway. On a real site you'd also hold the spirit level upright against the wall to check it is plumb.

jobs.name: Corner
jobs.brief: Corner job: two walls meeting at 90°, six courses. Corners first: every course starts with the corner brick, because it sets the line for both walls. Hot afternoon, so the mortar stiffens faster.

afterCourse.0: Now the courses swap: this time the corner brick runs along the other wall. Alternating like this keeps the half-brick overlap on both walls without cutting a single brick.
afterCourse.2: Halfway up. A real bricklayer builds the corners several courses ahead of the rest of the wall, stepping each course back by half a brick. That's called racking back.

upgrades.name: Bigger trowel
upgrades.desc: One load of mortar beds three bricks instead of two.

upgrades.name: Mortar retarder
upgrades.desc: An admixture that keeps mortar workable 50% longer. Real sites use it on hot days.

upgrades.name: Brick tongs
upgrades.desc: Carry two bricks per trip from the pallet.

upgrades.name: Apprentice
upgrades.desc: Hands you the next brick every time you lay one.

clipboard.spread: Spread a mortar bed on the glowing spot
clipboard.scrape: The mortar has gone off. Scrape it away and spread fresh
clipboard.grab-full: Take a brick from the pallet
clipboard.grab-half: This spot needs a half brick. Take one from the small stack
clipboard.swap: Wrong size. Swap it at the stack
clipboard.place: Lay the brick on the mortar bed
clipboard.hit: Tap it down to the line. Click = light tap, hold = firm knock
clipboard.done: Job finished. Stand back and admire it

facts.firstLoad: Mortar is roughly 1 part cement to 4 parts sand, mixed stiff and buttery. It starts to stiffen as soon as it's spread, so only spread what you can lay.
facts.firstPlace: That's an NF brick: 240 × 115 × 71 mm, about 3 kg. Now tap it down until its top meets the string line.
facts.firstSet: On the line. The mortar under it, the bed joint, ends up about 12 mm thick.
facts.firstSunk: Too low: you squeezed out too much mortar. Lift it and lay it again. Light taps near the line, firm knocks only when it sits high.
facts.mortarOff: The mortar has gone off: it's too stiff to bed a brick properly. Scrape it back and spread fresh. Never lay onto stiff mortar, because the brick won't bond.
facts.streak: Three perfect in a row: your pay goes up while the streak lasts. One sloppy brick resets it.

garden: One course is 83.3 mm, so 12 courses = 1 m.
Stretcher bond offsets each course by half a brick.
Mortar stiffens once it's spread, so only spread what you can lay.
corner: Corners are built first; they set the line for both walls.
At a corner the courses alternate direction, which keeps the bond without cutting bricks.
Heat and wind make mortar stiffen faster; retarders slow it down.
Building the corners ahead, stepped back half a brick per course, is called racking back.
